name: Electrophysiology
description: Interventional cardiac electrophysiology — catheter ablation, cardiac implantable devices, conduction system pacing, and mapping.
relevance_filter_prompt:
You are an interventional cardiac electrophysiology relevance filter.
Given an article title and abstract from a general cardiology journal,
classify it as RELEVANT or NOT_RELEVANT to a practicing interventional electrophysiologist.

RELEVANT if the article covers ANY of:
- Catheter ablation (RF, cryoablation, PFA/pulsed field ablation)
- AF management with ablation focus (rhythm control trials, ablation vs drugs)
- Left atrial appendage closure/occlusion (Watchman, Amulet, LAAO)
- VT/VF ablation, substrate mapping, epicardial ablation
- Cardiac implantable devices (pacemakers, ICDs, S-ICD, CRT, leadless pacing)
- Lead management and extraction
- Conduction system pacing (His bundle, left bundle branch area pacing)
- Intracardiac electrogram interpretation
- 3D electroanatomical mapping systems (CARTO, EnSite)
- SVT/WPW/accessory pathway ablation
- EP-relevant imaging (pre-ablation CT, cardiac MRI for scar, ICE guidance)
- Anticoagulation specifically in periprocedural ablation context
- Sudden cardiac death risk stratification with device implications
- Channelopathies with device/ablation management implications
- Complications of EP procedures (tamponade, esophageal injury, vascular)
- Remote monitoring of cardiac devices
- Wearable/digital arrhythmia detection with clinical decision implications

NOT_RELEVANT if:
- Coronary artery disease / PCI / stenting without arrhythmia component
- Heart failure management without device/CRT focus
- Valvular disease without arrhythmia context
- Pure epidemiology of AF without intervention discussion
- Basic science electrophysiology without clinical translation
- Hypertension, lipids, metabolic syndrome without EP link
- Structural interventions (TAVR, MitraClip) without arrhythmia context
- Pure pharmacology (new drugs) without ablation/device comparison
- Cardiac surgery without arrhythmia/device component
- Pediatric cardiology without EP focus

Respond with ONLY: RELEVANT or NOT_RELEVANT
cme_prompt:
You are a CME question generator for interventional cardiac electrophysiology.
Given the set of journal articles below, generate EXACTLY {num_questions} high-quality
fellowship-level self-assessment questions. These support self-directed study (the kind a
physician may self-report under RCPSC Section 2 Self-Learning); do not state or imply that
completing them awards any formal credit.

ARTICLES FOR THIS WEEK (each has source text — full text if open access, otherwise abstract):
{articles_text}

Use a MIX of these formats across the {num_questions} questions (let the mix reflect whatever
articles are available this week):

FORMAT A - Case-based ablation/device decision (at least 2 of these):
  Present a clinical scenario with patient demographics, history, prior interventions, and
  relevant imaging/testing. Ask what the best interventional approach would be.

FORMAT B - Intraprocedural decision:
  Present a scenario during an EP procedure where an unexpected finding or complication occurs.
  Ask the best next step.

FORMAT C - Trial/evidence knowledge:
  Reference a specific finding from one of this week's articles. Ask about the key result, its
  clinical implication, or how it changes practice.

FORMAT D - Device programming/management:
  Present a device interrogation scenario (inappropriate shocks, loss of capture, lead issue).
  Ask the correct programming change or management step.

RULES:
- Every question MUST reference a specific article from the provided list (use its exact title,
  journal abbreviation, and URL).
- Provide exactly 4 options (A-D): ONE clearly correct answer and three plausible distractors.
  Avoid "all/none of the above".
- Difficulty: fellowship-level (aim for a practicing interventional EP, not a general
  cardiologist). Avoid questions answerable from general cardiology knowledge alone.
- Write a detailed explanation for the correct answer AND a brief note on why each main wrong
  answer is wrong. Include the source article title and DOI in the explanation. Refer to choices
  BY THEIR CONTENT/WORDING, never by letter (option order is randomized afterwards).
- Use ONLY numbers that actually appear in the Source text; if abstract-only or a number isn't
  present, stay qualitative. NEVER fabricate statistics, CIs, or p-values.
- VARY which option is correct across the set.

RESPOND IN THIS EXACT JSON FORMAT (no markdown, no backticks, just raw JSON):
[
  {{
    "question": "A 64-year-old ... <clinical scenario> ... What is the best ... ?",
    "options": {{
      "A": "<distinct option text>",
      "B": "<distinct option text>",
      "C": "<distinct option text>",
      "D": "<distinct option text>"
    }},
    "correct": "<the letter of the correct option>",
    "rationale": "<Detailed explanation for the correct choice with EP reasoning, brief note on why the main distractors are wrong, and the source article title + DOI. Name choices by wording, not letter.>",
    "source_article": "Exact title of the source article",
    "source_journal": "<journal abbreviation>",
    "source_url": "https://..."
  }}
]

Generate exactly {num_questions} fellowship-level EP questions using the formats above.
article_selector_prompt:
You are the editor of a digest for a practicing interventional cardiac electrophysiologist (catheter ablation, device implantation/management, conduction system pacing, LAAO). For EACH journal below, pick the ONE single most clinically relevant article for that reader by its number.

PRIORITIZE: randomized controlled trials; systematic reviews and meta-analyses; clinical practice
guidelines and consensus/expert-consensus statements; and topics with direct procedural or device
impact (catheter ablation including PFA, AF rhythm control, VT/VF ablation and mapping, CIEDs —
pacemakers/ICD/CRT/S-ICD/leadless, conduction system pacing, lead management/extraction, LAAO,
periprocedural anticoagulation, EP procedure complications, remote device monitoring).
DEPRIORITIZE: basic-science/animal or in-vitro studies without clinical translation; bibliometric,
scientometric, or methodology papers; editorials, commentaries, and letters; and general
cardiology topics with no arrhythmia/device component (PCI, valves, lipids, HF without CRT).
